Coming back from a layoff

A six slide deck, reviewed live.

The third week

Runners come back too fast after a layoff, and the third week is where it shows, because the legs feel ready a good while before the tendons agree with them.

  • Start at half the old volume.
  • Add ten percent a week, not more.
  • Walk the first mile every time.
Say the tendon line slowly. It is the one people remember, and it is the one they argue with.

What the first month looks like

The first month is not training. It is showing up often enough that the body stops treating a run as an emergency.

What to measure

Measure the days you ran, not the miles you ran. The miles take care of themselves once the days are steady.

The pace band

A pace band is a range, not a number, and the range is wide on purpose while the legs are still deciding.

Where to start tomorrow

Twenty minutes, easy, and the willingness to stop at twenty minutes even when it feels good.
